scopeMarkdown:
Release `rayx_reactive` as **Git tags**: version **1.0.0**, one tag `vX.Y.Z` per release cut by release-plz from Conventional Commits, one root `CHANGELOG.md`, one GitHub Release per tag created by release-plz (no cargo-dist), consumers pinning `{ git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }`. Under the owner's **1.x policy** the crate stays on 1.x.x: breaking changes are released as `feat` (minor). Model: RayX.CLI's release setup, adapted by the shared library release shape and amendment 1 (both 2026-10-18); RayX.Dtcg's `dtcg-releases` is the pilot of the same template.

## In scope

- `release-plz.toml` (1.x policy: `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`, `semver_check = false`, a `Migration:` footer rendered in the changelog), `.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`. `ci.yml` keeps its triggers, push to `main` included.
- Version 1.0.0 (`[workspace.package]`, `Cargo.lock`); `CHANGELOG.md` with the configured header and `Unreleased` -> `## [1.0.0] - <push date>`.
- Local release-plz previews in scratch copies: initial release, patch, a `feat` that describes a break -> minor with the rendered `Migration:` note, no release.
- README and getting-started install text, `docs/releasing.md`, the contributing link, a `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` "Releases" section, the `rayx-reactive` skill's changelog guidance; all state the 1.x policy.
- Sprint s3 on GitHub: verify the secret and the tag ruleset, push (pre-approved) to release `v1.0.0`, check the run, the Release and `ci.yml`'s push run, and a consumer by tag.

## Out of scope

- crates.io publishing (manifests stay crates.io-ready; `documentation = "https://docs.rs/rayx_reactive"` stays though docs.rs will have no page); crate source, tests, benches, public API and `doc-examples` code; the `rclite` `branches`/`std` workaround (RayX owns it); RayX's switch to the tag and any RayX or RayX.CLI change; Renovate/Dependabot/GitHub Apps; local-override mechanisms; changes to `ci.yml`'s jobs.
- Creating the secret or rulesets (done by the owner, amendment 1 C).
- Memory promotion is closure work: a new repository decision (git-tag releases under the 1.x policy), the CHANGELOG clause of `knowledge/repository/rules.md`, and `knowledge/repository/state.md`'s stale "version 0.1.0 ... published to crates.io".

## Assumptions

- `ci.yml` is light CI (no e2e, benchmark or device lanes); it runs on pull requests (the release PR) and on pushes to `main`, with its job set unchanged (decision `d-ci-light`).
- `*Migration:*` notes come from a `Migration:` commit footer (git-cliff `commit.footers`), rendered by one template line: the only change to the CLI's `[changelog]`.
- release-plz is not installed locally; t03 installs the version `release-plz/action@v0.5` installs (0.3.172 on 2026-10-14) and amends the pin in the check script if it moved. cargo-semver-checks is not needed (`semver_check = false`).
- A first git-only release needs no PR: RayX.CLI's first run (2026-10-14) logged "treated as initial release ... already up-to-date" in `release-pr` and "released rayx-cli 1.0.0 (git-only)" in `release`.

## Owner prerequisites: done (amendment 1 C), verify only

`RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is a repository secret here (set 2026-10-18; the PAT RayX.CLI uses, created for "only RayX.CLI", so its access to this repository may still be missing); the tag ruleset "Release tags" (`refs/tags/v*`; `update`, `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`; no bypass; creation allowed) exists; the `main` branch ruleset blocks deletion and non-fast-forward with a bypass for `dXnSix`, the owner's credentials used for pushes. The owner pre-approved the first-release push and every release-PR merge (amendment 1 D).

## Deviations from the shared brief (found in the source)

1. The package lives in `crates/`, so the root changelog needs `changelog_path = "./CHANGELOG.md"`; one released package (no `version_group`/`changelog_include`); the version is `[workspace.package]`; no `[workspace.dependencies]` entry names an own crate.
2. `docs/02-getting-started.md` repeats the install text, with a `path = "../RayX.Reactive/crates"` snippet and a crates.io `0.1` promise; both go.
3. Repository rule and skill say to hand-write changes into `CHANGELOG.md` `Unreleased`; with git-cliff prepending under the header that breaks, so guidance becomes commit-driven with a `Migration:` footer.
4. `CHANGELOG.md` must start with the configured header byte for byte (git-cliff strips it before prepending), so the "unpublished (0.1)" sentence moves into the 1.0.0 lead line.
5. The CLI's comments describe cargo-dist; here `git_release_enable = true`.
6. The history before 1.0.0 holds three `!` commits and three `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers (`f492b02`, `8fb8579`, `6c2e2a6`); preview A proves they do not lift the initial release above 1.0.0, and later releases read only commits after `v1.0.0`.
constraintsMarkdown:
## Owner decisions (2026-10-18, with amendment 1), binding

- Git tags, never crates.io; manifests stay crates.io-ready. Consumers pin `tag = "vX.Y.Z"`; the `v*` ruleset blocks moving and deleting tags.
- 1.x policy: start at 1.0.0 and stay on 1.x.x while the owner is the only consumer. `fix`/`perf` patch, `feat` minor; a breaking change is a `feat` (or `fix`) whose body states the break and whose `Migration:` footer carries the consumer note. Never `!` and never a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. `semver_check = false`. The policy ends when a second consumer appears.
- One shared PAT as `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`. No local-override mechanism, no Renovate, Dependabot or GitHub App, no `rclite` workaround here.

## Push, PR and validation policy (owner, 2026-10-18)

- Focused local checks only: no dispatched CI runs, platform matrices or whole-workspace suites to close the epic (CLAUDE.md's "run before committing" list is not run). `ci.yml`'s automatic push run is checked green where it runs.
- Push straight to `main`, never a feature branch or implementation PR, always `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main` then `git push --force-with-lease origin main`.
- The release workflow lands in the same push as `1.0.0` (an earlier push would tag `v0.1.0`): nothing of this epic is pushed before task t08. That push and every release-PR merge are pre-approved; before merging a release PR, its proposed version must still be 1.x, it changes only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and its CI is green. A `2.0.0` proposal means a stray `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`: reword that commit (force push allowed) instead of merging.
- Pull requests only for releases. A tag made by hand (fallback) and closing a release PR still need the owner's go-ahead.
- Previews tag only scratch copies under ignored `artifacts-temp/agentx/reactive-releases/` with the push URL disabled; raw logs stay there.

## Repository rules

- Conventional Commits with scopes, never Claude co-author lines; this epic's commits use non-release types (`build(release)`, `ci`, `docs`, `chore(agentx)`) and never `!`.
- The crate stays standalone: never build, test or change RayX to prove this epic.
- Secrets are never printed or committed; `gh` is used for names and settings only.

requirements.title: Release automation with release-plz in git-only mode, on 1.x
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Conventional Commits drive the version, the changelog, the tag and the GitHub Release of `rayx_reactive`; nothing goes to a registry and nothing leaves 1.x.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`release-plz.toml` at the repository root:

- `[workspace]`: `git_only = true`, `publish = false`, `git_tag_enable = true`, `git_tag_name = "v{{ version }}"`, `git_release_enable = true` (release-plz creates the GitHub Release; there is no dist), `changelog_update = true`, `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"` and `semver_check = false`, each with a comment citing the 1.x policy (release-plz bumps the major for `!`, `BREAKING CHANGE:` or an API break cargo-semver-checks finds, and has no cap).
- `[[package]] name = "rayx_reactive"` with `changelog_path = "./CHANGELOG.md"` (the package lives in `crates/`; the repository keeps one root changelog). `[[package]] name = "rayx_reactive_doc_examples"` with `release = false`. No `version_group` or `changelog_include` (one released package).
- `[changelog]`: RayX.CLI's git-cliff configuration (Keep a Changelog header naming `rayx_reactive` and saying it is generated by release-plz; body heading `## [{{ version }}] - {{ timestamp | date(format="%Y-%m-%d") }}`; groups with scope markers; `trim`, `protect_breaking_commits = true`, `tag_pattern = "v[0-9].*"`, `sort_commits = "oldest"`; parsers that skip `chore(agentx)`, `chore(release)` and `chore(deps)` and group feat/fix/perf/refactor/docs/ci-build/test/chore) with one addition: under an entry, an indented `*Migration:* <value>` line for each commit footer whose token is `Migration` (git-cliff `commit.footers`).
- Comments explain every non-default the way the CLI's file does, without cargo-dist references.

Verified by `check-release-dry-run`: it asserts the two policy lines, release-plz loads the file (an unknown key or a template error fails every preview) and behaves as REL-3 states.

`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml` is RayX.CLI's workflow for this repository: on `push` to `main` and `workflow_dispatch`; jobs `release` (`command: release`) and `release-pr` (`command: release-pr`, with `needs: release` so the release PR is computed only after `release` has tagged, above all on the first push whose untagged history still holds `!` commits and `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers; as in Gpux), each guarded by `if: github.repository == 'rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive'`, with the CLI's permissions and non-cancelling concurrency groups, checking out with `fetch-depth: 0` and `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}`, the toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`, and `release-plz/action@v0.5` with `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}`. `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is the only secret; no step runs a shell command or tests. The header comment says why the PAT is needed (events made with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no workflows, so the release PR would get no CI), that release-plz creates the GitHub Release, and that tests live in `ci.yml`. `ci.yml` and `release-plz.yml` are the only workflow files.

Verified by `check-workflows` (structure) and `check-workflow-yaml` (no duplicate keys or syntax errors that GitHub rejects).

With the committed configuration, `release-plz update` in scratch copies of the working tree (tags only local to the copy, push URL disabled) behaves as follows:

- **A, initial release:** no `v*` tag (the history still holds pre-1.0 `!` commits and `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers) -> the version stays `1.0.0` and no file changes.
- **B, patch:** tag `v1.0.0`, then a `fix(signal):` commit -> `[workspace.package] version` and `Cargo.lock` say `1.0.1`; `doc-examples` stays `0.0.0`; the root `CHANGELOG.md` (not `crates/CHANGELOG.md`) gains `## [1.0.1] - YYYY-MM-DD` above `## [1.0.0]` with a `### Fixes` entry; the header appears exactly once.
- **C, a break under the 1.x policy:** tag `v1.0.0`, then `feat(collections):` whose body states the break and whose footer is `Migration: <note>` -> `1.1.0` (minor), a `### Features` entry without a `[**breaking**]` marker, and the `*Migration:* <note>` line. `!` and `BREAKING CHANGE:` are not used under the 1.x policy.
- **D, no release:** tag `v1.0.0`, then only `docs(readme):`, `chore(agentx):` and `refactor(signal):` commits -> the version stays `1.0.0` and no file changes.

Verified by `check-release-dry-run`.

requirements.title: Light CI on pull requests and pushes
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A release PR changes only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`; it runs the existing light CI, and pushes to `main` keep running it too (amendment 1 B).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` keeps its triggers `pull_request` and `push: branches: [main]` (adding `workflow_dispatch` is allowed, nothing else), keeps exactly its jobs `rust` (Ubuntu and Windows: fmt, Clippy, tests, wasm32 check, package), `docs`, `msrv`, `wasm-tests` and `macos`, and runs no benchmarks. So a release PR and each push to `main` run that light set and nothing heavier, and `release-plz.yml` runs no tests. No path filter is added.

Verified by `check-workflows` and `check-workflow-yaml`.

requirements.title: Version 1.0.0 and the first changelog section
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The first release is a clean 1.0.0 whose changelog section is the existing hand-written release notes.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`[workspace.package] version = "1.0.0"` in the root `Cargo.toml`, so `rayx_reactive` (which inherits it) is 1.0.0; `doc-examples` keeps `version = "0.0.0"` and `publish = false`; `Cargo.lock` is in step (`cargo metadata --locked` succeeds); `cargo package --workspace` still passes.

Verified by `check-version-changelog` and the final check `final-package`.

`CHANGELOG.md` starts with exactly the `[changelog] header` of `release-plz.toml` (byte for byte, so git-cliff can strip and re-add it). The `## Unreleased` heading becomes `## [1.0.0] - YYYY-MM-DD`, dated the day the version commit is pushed (sprint s3 corrects it if the push day differs). The sentence "The crate is unpublished (0.1); the breaking changes below are listed with migration notes for consumers." is reworded into a lead line of the 1.0.0 section (first tagged release; breaking changes are relative to the untagged 0.1 sources consumers used, each with a *Migration:* note). Every existing subsection (`### Delivery` ... `### API hygiene`) and all eleven *Migration:* notes are kept unchanged; there is no other release section.

Verified by `check-version-changelog`; preview B of `check-release-dry-run` proves release-plz prepends cleanly to this file.

requirements.title: Consumption by release tag and release documentation
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Users and contributors learn that the crate is consumed only by release tag, how a release happens, and the 1.x policy.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` (kept byte-identical) gain a short `## Releases` section before the AgentX block: Conventional Commits drive the version; the 1.x policy (breaking changes are `feat`, or `fix` for a fix, with the break stated in the body and a `Migration:` footer holding the migration note; never `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:`; it ends when a second consumer appears); `CHANGELOG.md` is generated (never hand-edited between releases); a release is merging the release PR after checking its version is still 1.x; the push policy (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, then `git push --force-with-lease origin main`; pull requests only for releases); link to `docs/releasing.md`. The `rayx-reactive` skill (`.claude/skills/rayx-reactive/SKILL.md` and `references/reactive-state-performance.md`) stops sending changes to an `Unreleased` CHANGELOG section and says the same about breaking commits.

Verified by `check-guidance`.

requirements.title: The first release on GitHub
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: v1.0.0 is cut by the release workflow on GitHub and consumable by tag. The owner's secret and ruleset exist and the push is pre-approved (amendment 1 C and D).

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
Before the push, verified (not created): `gh secret list --repo rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive` lists `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` (name only, never a value); `gh api repos/rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive/rulesets` and the ruleset's detail show "Release tags" active, targeting tags with `refs/tags/v*` included and the rules `update`, `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`, no bypass actors, creation not restricted; the `main` branch ruleset blocks deletion and non-fast-forward with a bypass for `dXnSix`, so the force-with-lease push works. A missing or different setting is reported to the owner, not fixed by the implementer.

Verified by the recorded `gh` output.

The epic's commits are pushed in one pre-approved push (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main && git push --force-with-lease origin main`) with the changelog dated that day. Then:

- the Release-plz run on that push is green: the `release` job logs `released rayx_reactive 1.0.0 (git-only)`, the tag `v1.0.0` points at the pushed `main` head whose `Cargo.toml` says `1.0.0`, and the GitHub Release `v1.0.0` (not draft, not prerelease) was created by release-plz with the `CHANGELOG.md` 1.0.0 section as its body (contains `### Delivery` and *Migration:* notes); the `release-pr` job reports the repository up to date and no release PR is open;
- `ci.yml`'s push run for the pushed head is green (a red run is a finding fixed forward with a 1.0.x patch; the tag is not moved).

If the run fails at checkout or push because the PAT lacks access to this repository, the implementer reports it to the owner (fix: add the repository to the PAT) and re-runs the failed run only after the owner says it is fixed, never retrying blindly. If release-plz cannot cut the first release, the by-hand fallback of `docs/releasing.md` cuts it with the owner's go-ahead and the deviation is recorded.

Verified by the run URLs and `gh release view v1.0.0 --json`, `git ls-remote` and `gh pr list` output.

A scratch consumer crate in a temporary directory outside the repository depends on `rayx_reactive = { git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive", tag = "v1.0.0" }`; `cargo test` resolves, builds and passes a test that uses `rayx_reactive::prelude::Signal`; its `Cargo.lock` source is `git+https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Reactive?tag=v1.0.0#<sha>` with `<sha>` equal to the commit `v1.0.0` points to on GitHub.

Verified by `check-consumer-tag`.
